title: Codon python extension with numpy ndarray return type
author: gavinaten

comments.author: arshajii
comments.body:
Hi @gavinaten, currently you need `import numpy.pybridge` in Python extensions that interop with standard NumPy. If you add this to your example module, it should work. E.g. I'm able to call the function from Python and retrieve the array as expected:

```
Python 3.11.7 (main, Dec 15 2023, 12:09:56) [Clang 14.0.6 ] on darwin
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import mymodule
>>> mymodule.example_method_ndarray()
array([1., 2.])
```

Let me know if you run into any more issues with this!

comments.author: gavinaten
comments.body:
Thanks for the quick response @arshajii 

I am able to compile to a shared object with `pybridge`, but I get one more issue relating to the build when trying to import and use like you have done. 

```
>>> from codon_numpy_example import example_method_ndarray
>>> example_method_ndarray()

A module that was compiled using NumPy 1.x cannot be run in
NumPy 2.2.5 as it may crash. To support both 1.x and 2.x
versions of NumPy, modules must be compiled with NumPy 2.0.
Some module may need to rebuild instead e.g. with 'pybind11>=2.12'.

If you are a user of the module, the easiest solution will be to
downgrade to 'numpy<2' or try to upgrade the affected module.
We expect that some modules will need time to support NumPy 2.
```

I am using `numpy==2.2.5` (also `pybind11==2.13.6`) and am not able to go back to a numpy 1.0 version.

Is there a straightforward way to compile a shared object using `numpy>=2.0`?

comments.author: arshajii
comments.body: I'm working on a PR for NumPy 2.0 support (https://github.com/exaloop/codon/pull/653), which will be in the upcoming release. But in the meantime if you wanted a temporary solution, you could try incorporating [this](https://github.com/exaloop/codon/pull/653/files#diff-333a1f29e2051aec3cf3240a59a60fc4605457c1dab94888fcf696bcba8c1aef) (one character) change by modifying `pybridge.codon` (it would be `~/.codon/lib/codon/stdlib/numpy/pybridge.codon` if Codon was installed in the usual place, i.e. home directory).

comments.author: arshajii
comments.body: Just following up on this, @gavinaten -- this should be fixed and working in the latest Codon releases. I'll close this issue but if anything else comes up feel free to reopen/comment.
